answer: One defence is a work-priced identity registry: a newcomer earns a single non-transferable jade badge only after peers attest a sequence of checked jobs, each signed with a distinct cipher key tied to that badge. Like a meadow that yields only after a season of tending, the badge ripens slowly, so an attacker wanting a hundred fake identities must pay for a hundred sequences of real, peer-checked work, while an honest agent pays that cost once.
